questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Philippines?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Philippines article.

questions.proof: The capital city of the Philippines is Manila.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Philippines?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Philippines on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “People” part of the Philippines article.

questions.proof: Even then, it is still has the most diverse ethnic groups in Asia, the other being Indonesia.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Philippines?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Languages” part of the Philippines article.

questions.proof: Filipino and English are the official languages.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “_____ (1521–1898) and the United States (1898–1946) colonized (controlled) the country and Palau, which is on the eastern side of the Philippine Sea.”

hints.nudge: The missing word is a name, not an everyday word. Only one of these names makes the sentence true.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Philippines article.

questions.proof: Spain (1521–1898) and the United States (1898–1946) colonized (controlled) the country and Palau, which is on the eastern side of the Philippine Sea.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The Spaniards came in _____, and brought with them Spanish culture.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the sixteenth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Culture” part of the Philippines article.

questions.proof: The Spaniards came in 1565, and brought with them Spanish culture.
